response: The EU's GDPR, effective since May 2018, fundamentally reshaped global data privacy by applying to any organization processing EU residents' data. Key provisions include the right to access, right to erasure, data portability, and explicit consent requirements, with organizations required to appoint Data Protection Officers and report breaches within 72 hours. Violations can result in fines up to 4% of global annual revenue or 20 million euros—enforced against major tech companies including Meta's 1.2 billion euro fine and Amazon's 746 million euro fine. While GDPR inspired similar legislation worldwide and established data privacy as a fundamental right, critics argue it creates compliance burdens that disproportionately affect small businesses, though enforcement inconsistencies across member states remain a challenge.
